Internal: where an Excel sheet's data begin

Source: R/io.R
dot-jst_excel_origin.Rd

readxl starts at the first row after skip = that holds anything and at the leftmost column that does, so a case's row and a variable's column in the sheet are counted from there (Session 365, for the stray-parts note). The first 200 rows after skip = are read as cells (col_types = "list", as .jst_excel_title_row() reads them); the columns left of the one they start in are then read down the whole sheet, since one cell there moves readxl's start.

Usage

.jst_excel_origin(path, sheet, skip)

Arguments

path, sheet, skip

As jload() read the sheet.

Value

list(row, col): the sheet row and column of the first cell readxl read; NULL when it cannot be found.
